body:
oliver: Quick design check — I'm proposing we split 'admission' out of the continuous-batcher core into a small contract so the batcher only cares about aggregating and executing batches. Main goals: simplify batcher invariants, make admission pluggable for dedicated vs hosted, and make headroom signals explicit to the KV cache.

mira: +1 to pluggable admission. can you sketch the contract? what's the minimal surface we need from the batcher side?

oliver: Minimal: admit(request) -> AdmitToken | Reject, where AdmitToken carries an opaque queue slot id and a 'headroomEstimate' (tokens/bytes) that downstream KV cache & kernel selection can use. Also include an optional priority hint.

devin: Are we mixing resource accounting and routing concerns? headroomEstimate seems fuzzy. how do callers compute it safely without peeking into the batcher internals?

ruth: That's the core tradeoff. If admit returns conservative headroom (small), we underutilize GPU. If optimistic, we can OOM or cause long latency spikes. Suggestion: admit returns two numbers: safe_headroom and optimistic_headroom + confidence flag.

oliver: Example proto sketch:
```
AdmitResult {
  status: OK | REJECT
  token: string // opaque
  safe_headroom: int64 // bytes of KV/activation we can guarantee
  optimistic_headroom: int64 // best-effort estimate
  priority: LOW|NORMAL|HIGH
}
```
This keeps batcher free to change packing without breaking callers.

mira: How do we propagate re-eval if the batcher compacts or evicts? token should allow a short cancel/refresh call, e.g. refresh(token) -> new headroom or invalid.

devin: Also need clear lifecycle: admit -> enqueued -> started -> finished/aborted. Batcher should expose simple callbacks or terminal calls so the admission plugin can reclaim reserved KV memory.

ruth: One more ops concern: metrics. If admission is pluggable we need per-admission-plugin telemetry (rejections, avg headroom error, refresh rate). Otherwise debugging is impossible.

oliver: Agreed. Plan: implement minimal contract above, add refresh and release endpoints, and instrument:
- admission.request_total{plugin}
- admission.reject_total{plugin}
- admission.headroom_error_histogram{plugin}

mira: Does this affect existing prefetch/kv-cache semantics? We currently assume the batcher will call prefetch once batch is ready. With admission we might prefetch earlier.

oliver: Prefetch remains the batch execution responsibility. Admission only signals how much we can safely reserve. But plugin might choose to eagerly prefetch if optimistic_headroom suggests it's safe.

devin: Concern: cross-runtime fallbacks. Hosted might want aggressive optimistic_headroom + fallback to smaller model; dedicated wants conservative. Pluggable admission solves this — but ensure default implementation favors safety.

ruth: Long-term refactor idea: separate a "resource manager" service that centralizes KV budgeting across multiple batchers on a node. Admission would query that service for headroom instead of per-batcher heuristics.

oliver: That matches my 2nd-phase plan. Phase 1: pluggable contract + default safe impl. Phase 2: centralized resource manager + admission plugins that call into it.

mira: Any API changes for clients (SDK/APIs)? I assume no — this is internal runtime wiring only.

oliver: Correct, no public API changes. All hidden in runtime config and the worker process.

devin: Implementation notes: keep the admit call cheap and non-blocking. Return a fast-path for admit_cached(token) to avoid per-request recompute when clients resend.

ruth: Ops checklist before rollout: 1) add feature flag, 2) enable plugin in staging, 3) run load test with synthetic headroom errors, 4) add dashboards and alerts for headroom_mismatch > X.

oliver: I'll draft an RFC with the proto and metrics, pinging @mira and @ruth for review. If no blockers we'll land a small shim first week and iterate.

scheduler-bot: automated note: created rfc/admission-contract-2635 in the repo and linked this thread.

mira: thanks — can you add a short example of how legacy admission maps to the new contract so we can validate behavior in canary?

oliver: Will do. short example in RFC will show current admit->always-safe headroom mapping and the new plugin that wraps it with refresh semantics. :+1:

devin: Cool. no objections from me. small nit: name the token field better than 'string' in proto (uuid + epoch maybe).

oliver: good call. I'll include token::{uuid, admit_ts} in the proto.

ruth: Sounds good. i'll prep dashboards after RFC lands. :eyes:

oliver: thanks all. closing this check-in — will post RFC link in this thread when ready.
